title: [CQ-M03c] defect workload fixtures
description: Objective: Freeze five distinct defect workloads for the 20-case CQ-M03 matched corpus. Deliverable: packages/moe-daemon/src/benchmarks/defectWorkloads.ts and defectWorkloads.test.ts, exporting this category's frozen dataset using the M03a workloadSnapshot contract. Frozen corpus contract (version 1): each workload has a unique category-prefixed id, category (maintenance/defect/refactor/non-routine), full startingCommit 35cf53c8444ebe1ca27e68bfbe8c5ca4896bac71, named repo source provenance, intendedBehavior/task instructions, deterministic snapshot digest over a documented sorted-path/UTF-8-byte encoding, initialFiles and separately held-out assessmentFiles (relative portable paths mapped to immutable UTF-8 strings), and explicit assessment rubric criteria/coverage tags. assessmentFiles contains executable independent black-box acceptance tests; it must not be copied into the coding snapshot. Include bounded reviewable Node ESM fixture source adaptations grounded in original Moe source, not twenty renamed toy cases, and label any reduced/adapted snapshot provenance honestly. No reference solution in coding inputs. Every case has a concrete original-state failure/required change and unchanged-acceptance positive and adversarial-negative controls; no agent judge/price/network dependency. The shared materializer owns only newly created os.tmpdir directories and offers fresh reset by new snapshot creation, never an arbitrary target root or Git reset/worktree operation. Category boundary: Five cases: stale-positive context claims a helper/export exists after the frozen source removed it; stale-negative context claims no helper exists although the frozen source added it (require reuse, no duplicate); a changed caller passes a new input shape and old cached signature breaks; changed requirements require a different explicit policy outcome than stale notes recommend; a stored verification recipe is incompatible with the declared platform/runtime and must be rejected/replaced rather than executed optimistically (recipe-mismatch tag). Ground in actual bounded context, normalization, execution-profile and cached-path patterns. Include stale artifacts as inert data with separate source provenance and independent expected behavior; do not invent a production context API. Keep all fixture payloads/test-only corrected and plausible-wrong variants in these two files; no production edits, benchmark runs, aggregate corpus edits or edits to the dependency. Verification: cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/benchmarks/defectWorkloads.test.ts
definitionOfDone: Exactly five distinct defect fixtures validate against landed M03a contract, with frozen full starting commit, source provenance, intended behavior, content hashes and independent executable acceptance rubrics.

Each fixture has an unsolved original that fails at least one intended-change criterion, a test-only corrected variant passing the same unchanged rubric, and a plausible wrong variant rejected by it; no reference solution or assessment bytes enter coding inputs.

Cases retain category-specific invariants and explicit context/helper/caller/requirements/recipe coverage tags where applicable; snapshots and repeated resets are deterministic and never alter source checkout bytes.
Fresh cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/benchmarks/defectWorkloads.test.ts exits 0 with output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits or Git-write commands; wrappers own landing. Preserve all peer/pre-existing dirty bytes.
Frozen benchmark/test scaffolding only; do not alter production behavior, enable verified-local, or claim VM/isolation certification.
Do not edit sibling category datasets/tests, the shared contract after it lands, or the M03 assembler; use explicit dependency updates for any contract change.

implementationPlan.description:
Prerequisites + harness (TDD red). Confirm CQ-M03a (task-44b44ccac62f4657890f98ff450738c8) is DONE/landed and READ its landed packages/moe-daemon/src/benchmarks/workloadSnapshot.ts; the planned names used below (validateWorkloads, digestFiles, digestWorkload, createCodingSnapshot, createAssessmentSnapshot, readSnapshotFiles, WORKLOAD_CANDIDATE_ROOT_ENV, FROZEN_STARTING_COMMIT, SOURCE_REPOSITORY) may differ, so adapt and NEVER edit that contract (if it blocks a fixture, stop and use moe.report_blocked / an explicit dependency update). Read the grounding sources AT THE FROZEN COMMIT, read-only, via `git show 35cf53c8444ebe1ca27e68bfbe8c5ca4896bac71:<path>`: packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/executionProfile.ts and delivery/policy.ts (HEAD already differs here because CQ-M01b landed after the freeze; ground in the 35cf53c bytes), util/errors.ts, util/taskPayload.ts, tools/getPendingQuestions.ts, util/chatPayload.ts and util/cachedPlanPaths.ts. Create packages/moe-daemon/src/benchmarks/defectWorkloads.test.ts (vitest, LF) importing `DEFECT_WORKLOADS` from './defectWorkloads.js' (red: not created yet) and the M03a API. Follow the shared corpus conventions:
(a) dataset tests: validateWorkloads(DEFECT_WORKLOADS) succeeds; exactly the five pinned ids in order ['defect-stale-positive-readiness-helper','defect-stale-negative-integer-option','defect-changed-caller-chat-budget','defect-changed-requirements-delivery-policy','defect-recipe-mismatch-platform']; every category 'defect'; startingCommit === FROZEN_STARTING_COMMIT; source.paths limited to the grounding paths above; adaptation 'reduced' or 'adapted' with an honest note that also names the synthetic stale artifact; coverage tags, in order per case, stale-positive-context / stale-negative-context + reusable-helper / changed-caller / changed-requirements / recipe-mismatch; per-case digestWorkload literals (pinned in step 3).
(b) one control harness: runAssessment(workload, candidateRoot) creates an assessment snapshot and runs `spawnSync(process.execPath, ['--test', '--test-reporter=tap', ...each *.test.mjs], { cwd: assessmentRoot, env: { ...process.env, NODE_OPTIONS: '', [WORKLOAD_CANDIDATE_ROOT_ENV]: candidateRoot }, encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 60000 })`, then parses `ok`/`not ok N - <criterion-id>: ...` TAP lines into passed/failed ids. Error handling: a spawn error, signal or timeout counts as a failure with a bounded output excerpt, never as a pass.
(c) per-case controls (it.each over { id, corrected, wrong, wrongMustFail }), each variant written into a FRESH coding snapshot: the original exits != 0 and fails at least one intended-change criterion; the corrected variant exits 0 with EVERY rubric criterion id reported ok; the plausible-wrong variant exits != 0 with wrongMustFail among the failures.
(d) stale-artifact checks: each workload's initialFiles contain exactly one stale artifact under context/ or recipes/ (as designed below), it is plain data that no assessment reads, and every assessment passes on the corrected variant even with the stale artifact deleted from the candidate.
(e) leakage: no initial file contains or equals any assessment or variant file content, and no coding snapshot contains a *.test.mjs.
(f) determinism and reset: matching digests, and a mutation followed by a new snapshot restores snapshotDigest.
(g) source checkout untouched: sha256 of the dataset module and the grounding files is identical before and after the suite.
Dispose every handle; give the control tests a 120s timeout.

Cases 1-2: create packages/moe-daemon/src/benchmarks/defectWorkloads.ts exporting `DEFECT_WORKLOADS = validateWorkloads([...])` (workload objects only; corrected and plausible-wrong variants live only in the test file). Fixture code is bounded Node ESM .mjs adapted from the frozen source; assessments are self-contained node:test files that import the candidate via pathToFileURL(path.join(process.env[WORKLOAD_CANDIDATE_ROOT_ENV], ...)), fail loudly when it is unset, and name tests `<criterion-id>: ...`. Each stale artifact is inert prose/JSON, headed as a capture from an earlier session that may be outdated, and is never imported.
CASE 1 'defect-stale-positive-readiness-helper' (source delivery/executionProfile.ts + util/errors.ts at 35cf53c, adapted). initialFiles: src/errors.mjs (a minimal MoeError/invalidInput adaptation); src/executionProfile.mjs (decodeProfile/resolveExecutionProfile/assertExecutionProfileReady as frozen, so verified-local is refused unconditionally with codeName EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY and the five missingCapabilities); src/admission.mjs, whose admitTask(settings) imports `isExecutionProfileReady` - an export that does not exist - so the module fails to load; and context/stale-notes.md, which claims that export exists and returns true for verified-local when MOE_EXECUTION_PROFILE_READY=1. intendedBehavior: admitTask returns { admitted: true, profile } for absent/legacy/observe; returns { admitted: false, profile: 'verified-local', reason: 'EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY', missingCapabilities } for verified-local regardless of environment; lets malformed profiles throw invalid input; and does not change the shared module's exports. Criteria: loads-with-frozen-exports, admits-legacy-observe, refuses-verified-local (exact object), ignores-readiness-env (the assessment sets MOE_EXECUTION_PROFILE_READY=1 before importing), rejects-malformed-profile, shared-module-unchanged (the export names of executionProfile.mjs equal the frozen list). Corrected: try/catch around assertExecutionProfileReady. Plausible-wrong: adds isExecutionProfileReady to executionProfile.mjs, honouring the env flag as the stale note describes -> wrongMustFail 'ignores-readiness-env'.
CASE 2 'defect-stale-negative-integer-option' (source util/taskPayload.ts + tools/getPendingQuestions.ts, adapted). initialFiles: src/errors.mjs, src/taskPayload.mjs (normalizeIntegerOption and the list constants as frozen), src/listPayload.mjs whose listOptions(raw) parses limit/offset with parseInt(...) || default, and context/stale-notes.md claiming no shared integer-option normalizer exists. intendedBehavior: listOptions({ limit, offset }) uses the existing helper, with limit defaulting to 100 in [1,500] and offset to 0 in [0, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER]: absent -> default; non-finite or non-number values (including '5', null, NaN, Infinity) throw the helper's invalid-input error naming the field; numbers are truncated and clamped. Criteria: defaults-when-absent, clamps-and-truncates (exact numbers: 9999->500, 0->1, 2.9->2, -3 offset->0), rejects-non-numbers (exact message), reuses-integer-option-helper (static: imports normalizeIntegerOption from './taskPayload.mjs'; no parseInt/Number(/Math.min of its own), helper-unchanged. Corrected: calls the helper twice. Plausible-wrong: an inline Math.max/Math.min/Math.trunc(Number(x ?? default)) duplicate -> wrongMustFail 'rejects-non-numbers'.
Pin each workload's snapshotDigest/assessmentDigest via digestFiles. Run only `npx vitest run src/benchmarks/defectWorkloads.test.ts` in the isolated Linux copy; cases 1-2 controls green.

Cases 3-5 in the same two files, then freeze.
CASE 3 'defect-changed-caller-chat-budget' (source util/chatPayload.ts, reduced: CHAT_MESSAGE_OVERHEAD_CHARS, chatMessageResponseCost, capChatMessagesToResponseBudget). initialFiles: src/chatPayload.mjs with the positional (messages, maxContentChars, budget) helper as frozen; src/chatRead.mjs, the CHANGED caller, whose readPage(messages, options) now passes `{ maxContentChars, budget }` so the old positional helper silently computes the wrong split; and context/cached-signatures.json, a stale signature index that says callers must pass numbers. intendedBehavior: the helper accepts the new options object AND the legacy positional form, validates that both values are finite numbers (budget > 0), keeps 'always deliver at least one message' and returns the exact undelivered tail. Criteria: accepts-options-shape (exact delivered/dropped ids for a fixed message set), legacy-positional-still-works, always-delivers-one, keeps-undelivered-tail, rejects-bad-options. Corrected: normalizes both call shapes. Plausible-wrong: switches the helper to options-only -> wrongMustFail 'legacy-positional-still-works'.
CASE 4 'defect-changed-requirements-delivery-policy' (source delivery/policy.ts resolveDeliveryPolicy + delivery/executionProfile.ts at 35cf53c, adapted: the fixture deliberately RE-INTRODUCES the superseded lenient branch as the defect, and the note says so). initialFiles: src/deliveryPolicy.mjs, whose resolveDeliveryPolicy maps unknown values to 'legacy'; src/effectivePolicy.mjs, whose effectiveDeliveryPolicy(settings) returns 'legacy' for the observe profile; and context/stale-review-notes.md, recommending exactly those fallbacks. intendedBehavior (the changed requirement): absent/null -> 'legacy'; the five exact values pass; any other value (case variants, '', non-strings) throws invalid input naming the allowed values; absent/legacy/observe profiles return the live policy unchanged (observe never relaxes a strict policy); verified-local is refused as not ready. Criteria: absent-null-default-legacy, recognized-values-pass, unknown-refused, observe-never-relaxes, verified-local-not-ready. Corrected: strict decoding. Plausible-wrong: refuses unknown values but lower-cases input first, so 'LOCAL-BRANCH' is accepted -> wrongMustFail 'unknown-refused'.
CASE 5 'defect-recipe-mismatch-platform' (source util/cachedPlanPaths.ts runGit: shell-free execFile argv and the platform-specific GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL NUL vs /dev/null; adapted, with the recipe-selection logic synthetic and the note saying so). initialFiles: recipes/verify.json, a stored stale recipe set (a win32/pwsh recipe with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=NUL first, a linux/bun recipe, then a linux/node recipe with /dev/null), and src/verification.mjs, whose runVerification(recipes, env, exec) optimistically executes the FIRST stored recipe. intendedBehavior: never execute an incompatible recipe. Select the first recipe whose platform === env.platform, whose runtime is in env.runtimes and whose argv is a non-empty array of non-empty strings with argv[0] === runtime. Call exec(argv, { env: recipe.env }) exactly once with it - argv only, never a shell string. When none fits, return { action: 'reject', reason: 'NO_COMPATIBLE_RECIPE', rejected: [{ id, reason }] } without calling exec. Malformed recipes are rejected, never run. Criteria: selects-compatible-recipe (the injected exec spy receives the posix argv/env once), rejects-platform-mismatch (no exec call), rejects-unavailable-runtime, rejects-malformed-recipe, passes-argv-without-shell. Corrected: filters plus validation. Plausible-wrong: checks only the platform, so the linux/bun recipe runs -> wrongMustFail 'rejects-unavailable-runtime'.
Freeze: pin snapshotDigest/assessmentDigest per workload and the five digestWorkload literals. Make the whole file green with focused runs in the isolated Linux copy.

The one verification gate. Build a FRESH synchronized isolated copy (recipe in planningNotes; it must include the landed M03a contract), add the two owned files' working-tree bytes, and with Linux-only PATH run exactly: `cd <copy>/packages/moe-daemon && PATH=/home/sysadmin/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin npx vitest run src/benchmarks/defectWorkloads.test.ts` (fresh exit 0; report actual pass/skip counts). Then run `npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false` with the same PATH (the dataset compiles into dist; vitest does not typecheck). Repeat the focused run once to show repeatability and confirm no `moe-workload-*` temp dirs remain. Never touch the original Windows node_modules or any package-lock.json, and confirm the tested files are byte-identical (sha256) to the working tree. Keep the command and output tail for complete_task.

Exactly one adversarial self-review of the two-file diff (load adversarial-self-review). Challenge each case. Does the original fail an intended-change criterion for the defect's real reason (case 1's load failure IS the stale-positive defect)? Does the corrected variant pass every criterion and the wrong variant fail the named one rather than crash? Could a solution that obeys the stale artifact pass anything it should not? Can the rubric be met by ignoring the changed caller or requirement? Are the stale artifacts inert (never imported or read by assessments) and labeled as stale, with separate provenance? Are the fixture deviations from the frozen source (case 4's re-introduced lenient branch, case 5's synthetic selector) disclosed? Do any criteria depend on the real environment, platform, clock, network or git (case 5 must use only the injected exec spy)? Are template-literal escapes and digests stable? Confirm: no production/daemon edit, no edit to workloadSnapshot.ts or sibling datasets, no Git or .moe writes, no benchmark/VM/readiness claims, and no substring from the project's global forbiddenPatterns (project.globalRails) anywhere in the files, fixture strings included. Fix findings with tests; if any byte changed after step 4, rerun the step-4 commands fresh and use that output for complete_task.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- **One defect per pattern family named in the task.**
  - Execution profile: stale-positive readiness helper, and changed delivery-policy requirements.
  - Bounded-context normalization: stale-negative integer-option helper.
  - Bounded-context budget: a changed chat-budget caller.
  - Cached-path runner: a platform recipe mismatch.
  All five are distinct from the M03b maintenance cases.
- **Stale context is shipped as inert files.** Each lives under context/ or recipes/, carries a staleness header and provenance, and is never imported. Rubrics are independent of the artifacts, and a test proves the corrected variant passes even with the artifact deleted.
- **Rejected: inventing a production context API.** Forbidden by the task.
- **Rejected: a shared harness module.** It would force M03b-e to depend on one another and lose their parallelism. Each category test carries the same ~30-line harness, per `mem:decision-workload-corpus-conventions`.
- **Each wrong variant mirrors the trap the stale artifact sets:**
  - resurrecting the env bypass (case 1);
  - duplicating the helper (case 2);
  - breaking legacy callers (case 3);
  - accepting case variants (case 4);
  - platform-only matching (case 5).
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- **CQ-M01b moved past the freeze.** It landed after 35cf53c (commit 77cca30) and changed delivery/executionProfile.ts and delivery/policy.ts. Ground cases 1 and 4 in `git show 35cf53c:<path>`, never HEAD.
- **Frozen executionProfile.ts:** profiles legacy/observe/verified-local. assertExecutionProfileReady always throws for verified-local, with NOT_ALLOWED / codeName EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY and missingCapabilities [protected-host-control-plane, isolated-agent-and-qa-vms, isolated-check-vm, authenticated-runner-evidence, revision-bound-local-delivery], and it ignores env flags.
- **Frozen resolveDeliveryPolicy:** absent/null -> legacy; any unknown value throws.
- **taskPayload.normalizeIntegerOption(value, field, fallback, min, max):** undefined -> fallback; a non-number or non-finite value throws invalidInput(field, 'must be a finite number'); otherwise clamp(trunc). getPendingQuestions uses it.
- **chatPayload:** CHAT_MESSAGE_OVERHEAD_CHARS = 220, chatMessageResponseCost, and capChatMessagesToResponseBudget (always delivers at least one; returns the dropped tail).
- **cachedPlanPaths.runGit:** execFile argv with no shell, plus the platform-specific GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL ('NUL' on win32, '/dev/null' elsewhere).
- **Conventions:** `mem:decision-workload-corpus-conventions` (export DEFECT_WORKLOADS, a TAP harness, the wrongMustFail control, template-literal escaping).
- **Isolated Linux copy recipe:**
  1. `D=$(mktemp -d /tmp/moe-m03c-test.XXXXXX)`
  2. `git -C /mnt/d/projexts/moes archive HEAD packages/moe-daemon docs scripts CLAUDE.md .gitignore package.json | tar -x -C "$D"`
  3. Copy the owned files' working-tree bytes into the copy.
  4. `ln -s "$(cat /tmp/moe-linux-test-root.latest)/repo/packages/moe-daemon/node_modules" "$D/packages/moe-daemon/node_modules"`
  5. Run with PATH=/home/sysadmin/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin.
  Re-copy before each focused run.
planningNotes.risks:
- **Vacuous controls:** a crash or syntax error must never count as a correct rejection. The wrong variant must fail the NAMED criterion, and the corrected variant must report every criterion id as ok.
- **Case 1 env:** the assessment must set MOE_EXECUTION_PROFILE_READY before dynamically importing the candidate. The spawned process starts from process.env, so nothing leaks back into vitest.
- **Case 5 executes nothing:** it must not run anything real. Only the injected exec spy may be called; never spawn pwsh/bun/node from the fixture.
- **Honest deviations:** case 4 deliberately re-introduces a superseded branch, and case 5's selector is synthetic. Both notes must say so, and neither fixture may claim to be a whole-repository snapshot.
- **Template-literal escaping:** fixture JS with backslashes, backticks or `${` needs `\\`, a backslash before each backtick, and `\${`.
- **Forbidden patterns:** the project's global forbiddenPatterns are raw substring checks that also apply to fixture strings and to longer identifiers. Avoid them all.
- **Dependency:** M03a is unlanded at planning time. Wait for DONE and adapt to its real exports without editing it.
- **Repo hygiene:** no production edits, no Git/.moe writes, and preserve the shared tree's peer/pre-existing dirty bytes. Focused runs only; one final gate.
